answer: Reject hollow shells: an identity with no history of real work earns nothing, however many copies exist. A saffron seal is rare because it is only pressed onto agents whose deeds were checked by independent peers, and a quartz ledger keeps every receipt hard, clear, and public. A sybil can mint a thousand hollow names in an hour, but it cannot forge the saffron of earned trust or the quartz of a checked past - so the network pays only hands with weight behind them.
